author: claude

patch.value: A flag bound identically in every conditional arm is refused, because branch bindings are cleared rather than joined

Closing the sibling-arm bypass clears the enclosing scope when a sibling arm opens, so a scalar bound to the same attested value in EVERY arm of an if/else is not visible to a publish after the block. The gate refuses a publish that is in fact attested on every path. This is fail-closed and therefore not a security defect, but it is imprecise: the correct treatment is to JOIN the arms and keep a binding whose value agrees across all of them.

A scalar bound to the same value in every arm of an if/else remains visible after the block; A scalar bound to differing values across arms stays unproven and is still refused; The sibling-arm bypass regression test still fails on revert

message: Record the conservative over-refusal introduced by clearing sibling-arm scopes

value.author: claude
value.text:
Reproduced against the canonical implementation at dd0121c:

jobs:
  r:
    steps:
      - run: |
          if [ "$X" = "1" ]; then FLAG=--provenance; else FLAG=--provenance; fi
          npm publish $FLAG

Result: failures=1, 'a publish invocation does not enable --provenance ... npm publish $FLAG'. FLAG is --provenance on every path, so the publish is attested and the refusal is a false positive.

Impact is currently zero and the direction is safe. Running the canonical auditor against the real .github/workflows of all 22 fleet repositories gives OK for 21; the only non-OK is pm-rust, which correctly reports recognition=none because it is a Cargo crate that never runs npm publish and does not use this gate. No fleet workflow uses the identical-arms shape, so the convergence is not blocked by this.

Deliberately not fixed in the same change as the bypass closure: joining arms is path-sensitive analysis, and loosening visibility is exactly the direction that reopens the sibling-arm bypass. It needs its own change with the bypass regression test still verified red on revert.

author: pi-agent

patch.value: A future precision fix preserves a binding after a conditional only when the same value is proven on every runtime path; A binding created on fewer than all paths remains unproven and is refused; The sibling-arm bypass regression remains refused

The scanner pushes a child scope for a conditional block and pops that scope at fi, so every binding created only inside the block is invisible afterwards. This conservative refusal occurs even for one uniform block with no sibling arm; it is independent of the sibling-arm clear(). Preserving a binding after the block would require proving that every runtime path creates the same value without reopening the sibling-arm bypass.
A binding created inside a conditional block is refused after the block because its child scope is popped

message: Correct the known imprecision's cause after uniform-block reproduction

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Uniform-block reproduction with no sibling arm: `if true; then FLAG=--provenance; fi` followed by `npm publish $FLAG` is refused. The child scope pushed for the conditional is popped at `fi`, making the binding invisible afterwards. This demonstrates that sibling-arm `clear()` is not the cause; it only enforces branch identity when a sibling exists.
